title: Make harvested crops plantable and cap what the player can carry

source_message: Accepted “What harvest-as-seed costs us in the simulation, honestly”.
result:
Harvested plantable crops now go directly into a single carried stock, with three plantable units per harvested crop. The pouch cap is 10 per species; the shipping bin keeps a separate plantable reserve of up to 10 per species before selling surplus. Players can take reserve stock back at the bin. A full pouch refuses a harvest without consuming the crop or energy. Old saves migrate without clipping stock. The 40-per-species grain-silo limit is tested as a future contract; a silo is not yet playable.

The game change landed on main in cc440b6 and the demo replay generator repair in 1cb5f01. Independent local main checks passed: 2,919 unit assertions, 1,005 integration assertions, robot replay, benchmark (121 µs/tick), gateway, writing, and deterministic replay-fixture regeneration. GitHub Actions passed: https://github.com/craklyn/tiny-farm-godot/actions/runs/35902919514. The earlier red CI run at demo replay generation remains in verification history; this repair fixed it without relaxing the gate.

recommend.question: What should a four-year-old see when she taps a ripe crop and has no room left to carry it?
recommend.answer: Show the shipping bin above the square.
recommend.why: The other candidates name the problem; only the bin names the fix, and the fix is a short walk she already knows how to make.
recommend.instead: The basket drawn overfull, which reuses the picture already on the HUD but tells her she is stuck rather than what to do about it.

subject: What a harvest is worth

prior_results.result:
All five checks are green: unit 2902 passed, integration 975 passed, the robot session replays to its own autosave, the one-gateway check passes, and the benchmark is inside budget. The work is in the worktree, uncommitted, as the house rules ask.

**What the game does now.** A harvested plant is the seed for the next one. The seed pouch and the crop basket were two piles of the same substance — one the planting drew from, one the shipping bin emptied — and they are now one pouch. Cutting a wheat puts a wheat back in her hand, so the farm she is given feeds itself and there is no wheat packet in the shop at all. Tomato and everything above it are still bought; every one after the first is cut from the last.

Two things follow from that, and both are the design rather than side effects. The bin now takes only what stands above a short row kept back for sowing — three — because a sale that took her last wheat would leave a farm that cannot be farmed. And the pouch has a limit of ten of one kind of thing: tapping a ripe crop she has no room for is refused, nothing is spent, and **the wheat stays standing on the square** to be picked up when there is room. The limit is computed from what is standing on the farm, never stored in the save, so a grain silo put down next to her raises it and no file can ever disagree with the buildings in front of her.

Old farms load. A save written before today comes back with its seeds and its crops added together, key by key, and an over-full stack is carried over whole rather than trimmed — an update that clipped a player's wheat to fit the new limit would be the update deleting her things. She simply cannot pick up an eleventh until she is back under.

**Three things worth your attention.**

The earlier attempt had written the sim and the docs but no tests for the new behaviour, so I added them: the full-pouch refusal leaving the crop ripe, the limit rising and falling with what is on the grid, the old-save merge, and a scenario that does it through a real tap on the real scene, because a passing test on the gateway says nothing about whether a child's finger can reach the refusal.

Harvest is the reward verb and it has never had a "no" before. It has one now, and there is no picture for it — every other refusal shows what she lacks above the tile, and "the pouch is full" has no drawing yet. That is the recommendation below.

I checked the claim that this change invalidates the recorded play sessions rather than repeating it: the two sessions pinned as reproducing their own end state contain no buying and no selling, so both still reproduce and the tests are green on them. Nothing was lost. What is true is that the archive can no longer be extended with a pre-change session that traded.

Two numbers in this — ten and three — are placeholders I picked, and they are filed as a question for you with a recommendation to leave them until somebody plays a week under them.
